exercise.title: 13th chords: a 7th chord with the 13
exercise.why: A 13th chord is a 7th chord with the 6th above its root added an octave up, so the 13 is heard as one high note a 7th above the chord's ♭7.

cells.text:
C13 is C7 with one more note stacked on top. Tap {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}} and {{b7}} from the lowest {{1}} on the staff below, then the {{6}} that comes after the next {{1}}: that note is the 13th.
Then tap the first {{b7}} and that upper {{6}}, one after the other. Those two notes are the sound of a 13th chord.

The circle below has the C chord of F major in the middle and the chords it can turn into around it. Press C7 on the circle, then C9, then C13.
Go between the three until you can say which note each one adds on top.

Press Play below to start the band: three chords, played twice. The second time, the 5 chord in the middle is a 13th chord and the other two stay as they were.
Once you hear the high note come in, look away from the chord boxes and call out "13" when it does.
Then listen in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to start the band again.
When you change the key, the chords are new but the 13th is still the 6th of the 5 chord, an octave up.
